Qualify first, then match the solution.

Dejavoo, PAX, Clover, Valor PayTech and CardPointe each solve a different merchant need. Each tab notes where that solution typically lands on the Grade scale, but a device never paints the full picture on its own. The merchant's environment, integrations and number of locations determine the final Grade.

Flexible acceptance

CardPointe

Flexible payment acceptance across channels. A cloud-based platform that works with a simple card reader, an existing setup or one of its own integrated terminals, so merchants add hardware only when it makes sense.

Start with

How does the merchant accept payments today?

Explore

In-person, online, remote and recurring needs.

Remember

Confirm what needs to connect before setting expectations.

Select a device to see the details.

Grade check

CardPointe can start as Grade 1 when the merchant uses the Virtual Terminal or a mobile reader with no system to connect. It moves toward Grade 2 when a terminal or reader connects to the merchant's software, and toward Grade 3 when that integration spans multiple locations.

Cash discount with SwipeSimple

PAX

Workhorse standalone terminals for merchants on Woodforest, Worldpay or Fiserv. Most PAX deployments pair the terminal with SwipeSimple's cash discount program, and the SwipeSimple B350 adds a pocket-sized Bluetooth option.

Start with

Does the merchant want a cash discount program, and where will they take payments?

Explore

Countertop, standalone and pocket-sized mobile needs.

Remember

Introduce SwipeSimple alongside the hardware, not as a separate pitch.

Select a device to see the details.

Grade check

On its own, PAX is Grade 1. Adding SwipeSimple, or the SwipeSimple Virtual Terminal for keyed and card-not-present payments, invoicing or scheduled recurring billing, adds setup and training and can move the opportunity beyond Grade 1.

Operations and POS

Clover

More than a terminal when operations need more. A 425+ app marketplace supports tableside ordering, loyalty, inventory and multi-location management.

Start with

What does the merchant need the POS to do beyond accepting a payment?

Explore

Restaurant, retail, apps, inventory and operational workflows.

Remember

Do not introduce complexity the merchant does not need.

Select a device to see the details.

Grade check

Clover is build-as-you-go. It can start as Grade 1 with a single device and grow to Grade 2 or 3 as the merchant adds apps, inventory and menus, online ordering, more devices or more locations. Match the first step to what the merchant needs today.

Straightforward terminals

Valor PayTech

Flexible terminal options for straightforward acceptance. Built-in dual pricing and surcharge features can reduce processing costs, and remote setup means no on-site tech visit. Debit cannot legally be surcharged, so these programs lower fees rather than eliminate them.

Start with

Where and how will the merchant take payments?

Explore

Countertop, customer-facing and mobile needs.

Remember

Fee-reduction conversations still require accurate qualification.

Select a device to see the details.

Grade check

Valor terminals typically start as Grade 1. Complexity grows when the merchant adds the ValorPay virtual terminal, e-commerce or invoicing, connects Valor to POS software through Valor Connect, needs Fiserv datawire provisioning or operates multiple locations.

Surcharge and cash discount

Dejavoo

Simple, reliable terminals for merchants who want surcharging or cash discounting. On-screen PIN entry, an integrated printer on most models and full WiFi/Ethernet/4G connectivity mean there is rarely a reason to hesitate on the device itself.

Start with

Does the merchant want to surcharge or offer a cash discount?

Explore

Countertop or wireless, printed or digital receipts and EBT needs.

Remember

Know the difference between surcharge and cash discount before you pitch it.

Select a device to see the details.

Grade check

At the surface, Dejavoo is Grade 1: a standalone terminal with few dependencies. It can become more complex based on the business and what it needs. Adding a virtual terminal through the iPOSpays gateway for keyed or phone payments, or connecting the terminal to the merchant's POS software through Dejavoo's SPIn semi-integration, adds setup and coordination.
